\begin{exercise} \end{exercise} 1. ch6:6-20

A connected Riemannian manifold is said to be extendible if it is isometric to a proper open subset of a larger connected Riemannian manifold.

  1. Show that every complete, connected Riemannian manifold is nonextendible.

  2. Show that the converse is false by giving an example of a nonextendible connected Riemannian manifold that is not complete.

\end{exercise}
